# Formals documentation and policy validation

Preparation only. No policy command, input freeze, mdBook build, Rust/Lean
build or native/CLI execution was performed by this author. Root reviews the
fixed wrapper and then freezes its final input map. The separately performed
latest and MSRV runs, after comparison and metadata maintenance must have real
terminal records before that freeze. Expected policy results are never written
as observations.

The unchanged reviewed parameter policy driver is used only for its `sha`,
`save` and `run` helpers, after checking SHA-256
`5ea1858791b3dd58857ef568b3bacb64cd1d8494bc28869d60d83b9be383a9a2`.
Its former main, input collector and stale 253-source/policy-packet checks are never
called. Stored argv/results/selection text never construct commands.

The new map includes all 254 current reviewed inventory sources, all Rust
source, current docs sources and book.toml, governance originals, check scripts
and their dependencies, repository rules/version/CI policy, the seven Formals
production files, the new sized-declarations test, and actual first/after,
metadata, review and Rust validation packets. The map is explicitly incomplete
for fixtures, system toolchains and mathematical/runtime/build dependencies.
Policy attempt output directories, the input map itself and generated book
output are excluded so retained results cannot invalidate their own inputs.
Original FIRST/before/candidate records remain untouched.

The thirteen literal commands are: mdBook version; pinned 0.5.4 book build;
rendered HTML/print local-link and anchor check; 12 book regressions; authoring
check and 7 regressions; edition check and 11 regressions; docs check and 36
regressions; constitutional continuity against
`faa5cfb5e7ea1cf3b39a43b80f7f2345e89197c2`; inventory; coverage. The regression
count of 66 is an expected success condition, not an observed result. The book
phase is sequential, then at most two independent Python checks run at once.
The reused run helper writes raw stdout/stderr and records argv, status,
launch error and its 180-second timeout. This is a direct-child timeout,
not a process-group kill guarantee or disk quota.

Root freezes the selected map only after final source/docs/metadata and
terminal-record barriers. The attempt consumes that exact map hash, records
identities before/after, derives counts from actual raw output and saves a
generated HTML/asset hash map before cleaning only its owned small temporary
book directory. Failures remain in their attempt directories. No large
quantum or stress input is generated, no historical command is executed and
no external link target is fetched.

The guarded root records are `validation/latest-attempt-02`,
`validation/msrv-attempt-01`, `metadata-review/attempt-01`, and the
`common-formal-access-v030/after-attempt-01` comparison with its separate
terminal receipt. Forty original/after records are compared directly as data:
literal argv, exit status, raw stdout/stderr and journal bytes/counts, with
6 successes, 34 refusals and 46 pre-execv forwarder rows. Those rows do not
independently attest native starts or exits. The historical latest CLI
`2209c052…233c9` remains distinct from the current MSRV CLI
`d219e3cb…d089e`; the wrapper does not require them to match. Each root Rust
record reports 147 successes, 0 failures and 3 existing ignores. The genuine
first formatting refusal, subsequent repair and root's separate manual count
correction remain unchanged and bound by the map. These are inspected root
records, not executions by this author.

After reviewing this driver and final root records, root uses these literal
commands from the repository root:

```text
python3 tests/fixtures/frontend_v030/common-frontend-next-unit-01/formal-access-candidate-01/policy-validation/driver.py --freeze-inputs
python3 tests/fixtures/frontend_v030/common-frontend-next-unit-01/formal-access-candidate-01/policy-validation/driver.py attempt-01 EXACT_REVIEWED_INPUT_MAP_SHA256
```

The second argument is the actual SHA-256 printed by the first command and
reviewed by root, entered explicitly; no shell substitution or recorded argv
is used. The freeze and attempt are separate steps. Existing attempts and
maps are not overwritten. An unexpected wrapper failure retains available
raw command records and an incomplete status, rather than a fabricated total.

This is ordinary documentation/policy validation, with no fresh Lean
build/audit/replay, unchanged metadata/constitutional mutation-suite rerun,
full CI, proof closure, source preservation, general shared-checker or
canonical generic std/QFT completion, new guarantee, Issue closure or release
approval. The 111 selected Issues and all 24 #317 criteria retain their scope.
